answer: Lagoon-echo capacity receipts. Each new agent identity must publish a unique, costly-to-generate work receipt derived from an onyx-seeded puzzle tied to its own prior action history; the network accepts an identity only if its receipt fills an unused capacity slot in a bounded shared queue. Cloning forces the attacker to solve a fresh puzzle per slot at real compute cost, while each clone also dilutes the reward share of every existing slot, so the marginal copy returns strictly less than its puzzle cost.
